baseline:
B
Root-finding is the process of finding the roots (or zeros) of a function, which are the points 'x' where the function's value f(x) is equal to 0. This corresponds to where the function's graph crosses the x-axis.

B
Newton's Method works by starting with a guess, finding the tangent line to the function at that point, and then using the x-intercept of that tangent line as the next, better guess for the root. The slope of the tangent line (the derivative) is critical for calculating this x-intercept.

C
Newton's Method uses the x-intercept of the tangent line at the current guess as the next, improved approximation for the root.

C
A Newton's fractal visualizes basins of attraction. All points (initial guesses) within a region of the same color will converge to the same specific root of the function when Newton's method is applied.

B
This statement accurately describes the sensitive dependence on initial conditions, a key feature of chaos. The complex fractal boundaries show that a tiny shift in the starting guess can cause the method to converge to a completely different root, making the outcome for points near these boundaries unpredictable.
